items.followUp: Why are the elements of group 13 called p-block elements?

rubric.why: The differentiating electron in group 1 and group 2 elements enters an s subshell.
rubric.description: Identifies the subshell receiving the differentiating electron.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the last or differentiating electron enters an s subshell.

rubric.why: Group 1 elements have an ns1 outer configuration and group 2 elements have an ns2 outer configuration.
rubric.description: Gives the outer electronic configurations that identify these as s-block elements.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating the ns1 and ns2 configurations for groups 1 and 2, respectively.

modelAnswer: The last (differentiating) electron of group 1 and group 2 elements enters an s subshell.
Their outer electronic configurations are ns1 and ns2, respectively; therefore, they are called s-block elements.

items.followUp: Why does atomic size increase down a group?

rubric.why: Additional electron shells down a group increase atomic size and the distance of the valence shell from the nucleus.
rubric.description: Identifies the increased atomic size or valence-shell distance down the group.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that atomic size or the distance of the valence shell from the nucleus increases.

rubric.why: Increased distance and shielding weaken the nucleus's attraction for a shared pair of electrons, lowering electronegativity.
rubric.description: Explains the reduced attraction for shared electrons and its effect on electronegativity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking increased distance or shielding to weaker nuclear attraction and decreased electronegativity.

modelAnswer: Down a group, atomic size and the distance of the valence shell from the nucleus increase, and shielding increases.
The nucleus's attraction for a shared pair of electrons decreases; therefore, electronegativity decreases.

items.followUp: Differentiate between a polar covalent bond and an ionic bond.

rubric.why: A difference in electronegativity causes unequal sharing of the electron pair in a polar covalent bond.
rubric.description: Describes electron sharing in a polar covalent bond.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the electron pair is shared unequally in a polar covalent bond.

rubric.why: Equal or nearly equal sharing in a non-polar covalent bond means that poles do not develop.
rubric.description: Contrasts electron sharing in a non-polar covalent bond.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that sharing is equal or nearly equal, or that no poles develop.

modelAnswer: In a polar covalent bond, bonded atoms with different electronegativities share the electron pair unequally, producing partial charges or poles.
In a non-polar covalent bond, the atoms share the electron pair equally or nearly equally, so no poles develop.
